neighbours.label: 'unable / unsure / not sure / would like' in a reader-directed condition ('If you are unable to ...')
fire: If you are unable to attend the meeting, please send a written apology.
If you're unsure which form to fill in, ask at the front desk.
If you are not sure about the dosage, check with your pharmacist.
If you’d like a vegetarian meal, tick the box on the booking form.
If you cannot find your ticket, the office can print a new one.
If you are unsure of the route, follow the yellow signs from the station.
If you would like to volunteer, leave your name with the coach.
Guests who are unable to climb stairs should request a ground-floor room.
quiet: If you are attending the meeting, please bring a written report.
If you're filling in the form, use black ink and capital letters.
If you are taking the tablets, check with your pharmacist every month.
If you ordered a vegetarian meal, it will arrive with a green label.
If you find your ticket, the office can cancel the new one.
If you are walking the route, follow the yellow signs from the station.
If you volunteered last year, leave your name with the coach again.
Guests who are staying three nights should request a ground-floor room.

notes: Card: ' unable' x5, ' unsure' x4, ' would'/'’d' x9, ' sure' x3, ' cannot' x3, all after 'If you (are)'. Near misses keep 'If you are' with other predicates.
